proverbs.text: Two thousand drinks in the cellar will not walk to a thirsty miner.
A barrel you cannot reach is only a very large rumor.
Never climb a tree you cannot climb down while thirsty.
The tree branch is a fine view and a poor tavern.
Count your armor stands before you count your soldiers.
One throne is a seat. A hundred thrones is a policy.
The order you forgot to cancel will outlive you.
A burrow called Safety has never once read its own sign.
Thirty levels down is far from danger, and farther from help.
What goes into the garbage pit should not be asked to come back out.
Throw refuse in, or haul it out. Never both on the same afternoon.
The mood always wants what the jeweler finished yesterday.
Do not cut every gem; somewhere a fisherdwarf is about to have a feeling.
When the child stares at the loom, start growing plant fiber.
A militia of one is still a militia, if you do not count it.
The captain is never off duty in spirit, only in every other way.
Nine empty places in a squad make very quiet drills.
An office nobody takes is the only office that never fails.
The mayor's paperwork is heavier than the mayor's hammer.
A production order violation is just a wish with a seal on it.
The liaison has much to share; mostly the word 'much'.
Ask the liaison for gossip, receive an import agreement.
A liaison asking double for rings is not trading; he is courting.
Smooth one wall and the Overseer will see a mountain of walls.
Sixteen thousand jobs and three smoothers: that is called a career.
Four hospitals and two doctors is two hospitals of waiting.
Gather plants in the rain, and you gather mostly rain.
A fortress is only as wet as its driest dwarf is thirsty.
The gods blink; the dwarf finishes the same sandwich twice.
After the Great Rewind, nobody admits to remembering the first try.
Every new fort is just the old fort with fresh ignorance.
Leave an artifact behind and a goblin will dust it for you.
An artifact left in a fallen fort is a gift to the next owner.
Forty claimants and still no one wears the greaves.
Goblins take a fort the way rain takes a hat: rudely and for good.
Total war with one goblin, skirmishes with another: a busy calendar.
An army with a mad name has never been described as calm.
Refugees carry little; their stories are the heavy part.
Sixteen friends and two enemies; the enemies visit more often.
Peace is a treaty; war is a visit; the liaison wants both in writing.
The crooked horror does not hurry; it has never needed to.
If the beast is coming up the stairs, the stairs were a mistake.
Mist from the pumps: happiness you can wring out of your beard.
A windmill turns whether or not anyone knows why.
Build the cistern before the thirst, not after the funeral.
The catacombs are the only rooms that never complain about the smell.
An execution tower is very tall for a building nobody visits twice.
A sock of silk scrap can hide a whole shortage of cloth.
The weaver who waits for the loom room will wait in the next life.
A hundred gems will not pour a single mug.
Meat Watch, day forty: hope is a plump helmet in disguise.
A dozen dogs and no meat: the dogs noticed first.
Eight hundred loose stones and not one of them is a sandwich.
Twenty farm plots can still feed a famine if nobody plants them.
Seventeen plants for ten dwarves is arithmetic, not dinner.
Day thirty of famine: everyone becomes a philosopher.
Better a fort of stone than a fort of armor stands.
Nobody sits on a throne on purpose after the fortieth throne.
The camera follows the elf; the elf believes it is famous.
Wherever the merchant walks, the spectator's eye walks too.
If the camera jumps away mid-sentence, run where it went.
A dwarf in the hospital is a patient; in the burrow, a statistic.
The champion's chair stays warm only because the cat likes it.
No sheriff, no hammerer, no trouble on paper.
Vacant offices make the quietest council meetings.
A fort with no dungeon master has very well-behaved animals.
The Overseer's plan is sound; it is the dwarves who are noisy.
Trust the strategy, and keep a mug hidden behind your back.
The Overseer counts the barrels; the dwarf counts the steps to them.
A newspaper outlives its fort, and so do its corrections.
A town that changes hands keeps its potholes.
Reclaim the old hall, and you also reclaim its old bills.
Do not die of thirst on the job; it ruins the job.
A dwarf who is fey borrows everything and returns a masterpiece.
The possessed weaver makes no small talk.
Three forts in one world is not bad luck; it is a tradition.
When in doubt, smooth it. When not in doubt, the Overseer smooths it.
The best armor stand is the one you never had to build.
Every refuse hauler is a hero until the pit is full of heroes.
A safe room is a room nobody has tested yet.
Speak softly to the Overseer, and carry your own water.
If the plan is strange, wait a season; it will become stranger.
The deepest mine is dug by the dwarf who was told to stop.
Remember {past_fort}: it {past_fort_fate}, and it had plenty of barrels.
{record} is a boast at the tavern and a warning in the ledger.
{past_fort} lasted {past_fort_years}; its mistakes will last longer.
Never trust a {enemy_race} who says the war is a skirmish.
Every ghost at Searabbeys is still waiting for its meat.
Two thousand drinks at Searabbeys, and one dry miner. Lift the mug.
The Nuanced Hamlet waits at Searabbeys, nuanced and unvisited.
A silver mace remembers Quakefocus better than Quakefocus does.
One thousand nine hundred eighty-one stands, and not one helmet.
The Amusing Duties amuse only those who never held them.
The Oily Boots will reclaim Scaldedarch, slowly and slipperily.
Shadyghosts is named honestly, which is rare in a place name.

almanac.text: Thirst paradox season begins. Before walking to the cellar, confirm the cellar is not up a tree.
A good week to cancel old work orders. A bad week to discover how many there were.
Armor stands are in abundance this year. Astrologers advise standing near one for luck. Any one.
The stars favour smoothers. The stars do not have to do the smoothing.
Omens favour gem cutting. Omens also warn that someone, somewhere, will want them rough.
{moodname} has taken a workshop. The almanac advises against cutting, finishing or tidying anything for a week.
Plant cloth is lucky this week, particularly for anyone under the age of twelve with a far-off look.
The Burrow of Safety is unfavourable this season. So was it last season. Check the stairs.
Garbage pit: neutral omens for dumping, very poor omens for retrieving.
The liaison is due. Expect much to share and an import agreement to sign. Then sign nothing.
Year {year}: the omens predict a strongly worded charge of production order violation.
The militia remains off duty in {season}. The almanac forecasts no change, to two decimal places.
A favourable week to be appointed sheriff, if anyone would like to be appointed sheriff. Anyone?
The pumps turn in harmony this week. Stand in any spray you can find and feel better about everything.
Windmill omens are turning. Then turning back. Windmill omens are mostly turning.
Catacombs report full occupancy. The almanac recommends a new wing, ahead of schedule.
{deadname} is entered into the great ledger this week. Plant something near the tomb; it is what they would have hauled.
Goblin moon rising. Close the gates early and hide the good mugs.
Skirmish weather this week, our sages note, which in a goblin war is any weather.
Crooked horror sightings are on the rise. Travellers: avoid anything crooked, and anything horrible.
{weather} on the surface, which the Overseer reads as an excellent day for gathering plants across the whole map.
Rain falls on the herb gatherers, who have been sent to the far edge of the map for one strawberry.
Snow on the surface. The Overseer's plant-gathering orders are, sadly, not paused for snow.
Clear skies: a fine day for climbing a tree. The almanac urges you not to.
Spring: trees bud, branches lengthen, and miners look upward with dangerous curiosity.
Summer heat dries the throat. Locate your nearest barrel now, while you still remember the way.
Autumn harvest. Count the plants, then count the dwarves, then do the arithmetic before history repeats.
Winter: the caravan road ices over and the liaison arrives regardless, sliding in with much to share.
The constellation of the Hundred Thrones rises tonight. Nobody is sitting in any of them.
The world may blink this week. If it does, finish your sentence again from the top.
A Great Rewind is neither forecast nor ruled out. Keep your work saved in your head.
Lucky gem: any rough one, kept somewhere secret for the next mood.
Lucky material: plant cloth. Unlucky material: plant cloth you used for socks yesterday.
A fine week for hospitals. Please staff one before getting injured.
Children are restless. The almanac recommends teaching them a craft before a mood teaches them one.
Refugees on the roads this {season}. Set an extra place at the table; set two if they are tall.
Execution tower: unfavourable omens all year round. That is rather the point of it.
Year {year} in {world}: one more fortress, one more chance to place the still near the beds.
A good week to build a ladder down from every tree. Nobody will understand why. Do it anyway.
Unlucky colour: refuse brown. Lucky colour: the blue of a full cistern.
Omens favour the mayor's mandates this week. Omens do not favour whoever has to fulfil them.
The camera's eye roams the halls this week. Comb your beard; it may follow you to dinner.
Elves passing through. The almanac advises hiding the wooden furniture and both armor stands you kept.
The {past_fort} comet passes overhead this week. That fort {past_fort_fate}; look up and be kind.
{past_fort} Memorial Week: drink one extra mug for a fort that lasted {past_fort_years}.
Anniversary of {record} at {record_fort}. Celebrate by not making any more of them.
Toast {monarch} this week with something from the cellar. The monarch will never know, which is the best kind of toast.
{liaison} is expected. Polish the meeting room, hide the rings, and practise saying 'no' in a friendly voice.
{enemy} are on the march somewhere. The almanac suggests being somewhere else.
{civ} feast day, possibly. Nobody has the calendar. Feast anyway; it is the safe choice.
Lucky number: 1,994. Unlucky number: 0, the number of mugs the Searabbeys miner actually drank.
The anniversary of the 1,981st armor stand of Quakefocus approaches. Celebrate by not building one.
The Sable Nights are lengthening. Something in them, namely Thone Nìnoana, is lengthening too.
The Vice of Fins is reported near Padtufted again. Padtufted has asked to be reported somewhere else.
The Chaste Cudgel's reclamation of Tametomb is a year older. Send a cake. Send a guard with the cake.

On this day, a miner was found dead of thirst in a fort holding nearly two thousand drinks. The barrels declined to comment.
On this day, a runaway work order completed its two-thousandth armor stand. Nobody owned any armor.
On this day, a fort carved its hundredth spare throne. It had no monarch and, briefly, nowhere to stand.
On this day, the smoothing queue passed sixteen thousand jobs. Its three smoothers were informed by a very long scroll.
On this day, a fort declared 'famine, day 32'. Seventeen plants were divided among ten dwarves, with arguments.
On this day, a fey carpenter died of thirst beside a hundred and fifty rough gems. Gems, it turns out, are not a beverage.
On this day, a possessed weaver waited for the loom room so long that the loom room outlived him.
On this day, seven silk scraps successfully hid an entire cloth shortage from the Overseer.
On this day, a fort opened its fourth hospital. It joined the second hospital in having no doctor.
On this day, a miner died of thirst on a tree branch. Arborists now list 'miner' as a rare fruit.
On this day, fifteen dwarves sheltered in the Safety burrow, thirty levels down. A forgotten beast used the stairs.
On this day, eight haulers were lost carrying refuse out of the garbage pit while more refuse was thrown in.
On this day, a dwarven child was taken by a strange mood and demanded plant cloth. Nobody had any. Nobody had asked.
On this day, a moody fisherdwarf demanded rough gems, one day after the last was cut. Timing, the jeweler said, is everything.
Did you know? The ring of misting pumps is the least practical and most beloved object a fort can build.
On this day, a militia was founded with one captain and nine empty places. It has been off duty ever since.
On this day, a mayor filed the first charge of 'production order violation'. The defendant was the entire fortress.
Did you know? The offices of sheriff, hammerer, dungeon master and champion have, between them, a combined staff of nobody.
On this day, the world blinked. Every dwarf in {fort} repeated the last hour and agreed not to mention it.
Did you know? Dwarves call the times the world stopped and restarted 'the Great Rewinds'. Nobody remembers how many there have been.
Did you know? {fort} currently holds {drinks} drinks. Historically, that has never once stopped anyone from dying of thirst.
On this day in {year}, {citizen} walked past a full barrel without drinking. Historians are monitoring the situation.
Did you know? {fort} has {farms} farm plots. Forts have kept a Meat Watch going for years with fewer.
Did you know? {masterwright} made {masterwork}. A runaway work order would have made two thousand of them.
Did you know? {fort} is home to {cats} cats. Not one of them has ever been put on a work order, despite the Overseer's interest.
Did you know? There is a great deal of {stone} in {fort}. Historians recommend counting it before it becomes a record.
On this day, the camera followed an elf merchant for forty minutes. He bought nothing. It was riveting.
On this day, an execution tower was completed. The architects described it as 'tall and morally ambiguous'.
On this day, a miner smoothed his own bedroom four times because the order kept coming back. He now lives in a mirror.
Did you know? The most-claimed artifacts in {world} are the ones nobody can reach. Claiming is cheaper than travelling.
On this day, a refuse hauler asked who was throwing things into the pit. The answer arrived from above.
On this day, a fort built a burrow and named it 'Safety'. Forgotten beasts across the caverns took note.
On this day at Searabbeys, Bomrek Enshalcatten was found dead of thirst while the fort held 1,994 drinks.
On this day, The Torments of Hating occupied Searabbeys, evicting The Distant Letter, who had only just unpacked.
On this day at Quakefocus, the 1,981st armor stand and the 148th throne were finished in the same week.
On this day, Claspedserpent was forged: a silver mace, now the pride of the ruins of Quakefocus.
On this day in year 68, The Amusing Duties were lost at Roughnessslaps. About forty-eight figures have claimed them since.
On this day, The Crazed Hex drove refugees out of Padtufted, Pulledrained and Ironcrowds in a single season.
On this day, The Chaste Cudgel reclaimed Tametomb under Bomrek Thimshursåkzul. The first job was dusting.
On this day, Iden Loloklolor asked for rings at 210% of their value. He described it as friendship.
Did you know? Searabbeys, Quakefocus and Creaturemirrored all stand in The Enchanted Planes. It is a very well-visited world.
On this day, the elf Mame Ayathemiyi was abducted at Nobledessert. Elves called it a tragedy; goblins called it a schedule.
Did you know? The crooked horror Omo Fewethauyira lives near Shadyghosts. Locals say the name is not even its scariest feature.
