reviews.head: The Armor Stand Galleries
reviews.body: Nearly two thousand armor stands in perfect rows, holding nothing, guarding nothing, meaning nothing. Critics call it minimalism. I call it a work order nobody cancelled. Haunting, in the way a very full storeroom is haunting.

reviews.head: The Throne Hall, All Hundred-Odd Seats
reviews.body: A throne room with over a hundred thrones and no monarch. Every seat is the seat of power, so no seat is. I sat in eleven. Each one made me feel slightly more important and considerably more confused.

reviews.head: The Safety Burrow, Thirty Levels Down
reviews.body: Spacious, quiet, deep, and reachable by a staircase that also works for forgotten beasts. Whoever named it had a fine sense of irony and no sense of stairs. One star, for the sign, which is beautifully engraved.

reviews.head: The Mist Ring of Pumps
reviews.body: A circle of pumps that sprays water into the air for no reason except joy. Wildly impractical. I stood in it for an hour and forgot every grudge I own. Then I remembered them, damp. Five stars, one towel.

reviews.head: The Execution Tower
reviews.body: Tall, sober and elegantly proportioned, with a staircase that only ever seems to go up. The view from the top is the best in {fort}. I recommend enjoying it as a visitor rather than as a guest of honour.

reviews.head: The Garbage Pit, Revisited
reviews.body: A bold open-plan design: things go in from above, and haulers go in from below to bring them out again, at the same time. The concept is daring. The execution is literal. Bring a helmet and a strong opinion.

reviews.head: The Catacombs
reviews.body: Long, cool corridors of slabs and niches, beautifully quiet. The residents never complain and never move, which makes them the finest neighbours in the fort. Ghost activity moderate. Echoes excellent.

reviews.head: Four Hospitals, Two Doctors
reviews.body: Four handsome hospitals, each with beds, splints and lovely smoothed walls. Two of them also have a doctor. I was treated in one of the others by a very sympathetic bucket. Architecturally sound; medically optional.

reviews.head: The Cistern
reviews.body: A great dark lake under the fort, still and full. After everything our forebears went through with thirst, it is the most reassuring room I have ever entered. I would sleep beside it if the cats allowed.

reviews.head: The {stone} Gallery
reviews.body: An entire corridor of {stone}, smoothed to a mirror finish by a team who were given no other choice. You can see your own face fourteen times. None of them look rested.

reviews.head: The Ruins of {past_fort} (A Retrospective)
reviews.body: I toured the plans of {past_fort}, which lasted {past_fort_years} and {past_fort_fate}. Sensible halls, a decent dining room, and the stills a very long walk from the beds. That walk explains a great deal.

reviews.head: 'Two Thousand Drinks: A Thirst Story'
reviews.body: A gripping account of a miner who died of thirst in a fort awash with drink. The author spends three hundred pages asking how. The answer, on the last page, is 'stairs'. Devastating. Have a mug nearby.

reviews.head: 'Famine, Day 32'
reviews.body: A founding diary: seventeen plants, ten dwarves and one hundred pages of increasingly philosophical hunger. Chapter twelve is just a drawing of a sandwich. It is the best chapter.

reviews.head: 'There Is Much To Share' by an Outpost Liaison
reviews.body: A liaison's memoir. Every chapter opens with the title and closes with an import agreement. The middle is mostly about rings, at prices I will not repeat. Shares much; says little.

reviews.head: 'Off Duty' by a Militia Captain
reviews.body: A lonely book about command. The author describes drills with nine empty places in moving detail. I wept at the roll call chapter, which is one name long. Brief, brave and still not on duty.

reviews.head: 'Smooth: Sixteen Thousand Walls'
reviews.body: A smoother's memoir, written one wall per page. There are sixteen thousand pages. I read eleven. They were very well finished. The binding is, inevitably, smoothed.

reviews.head: 'Up a Tree' (Cautionary Tales for Miners)
reviews.body: Picture book, intended for children, read by miners. A miner climbs a tree. The miner does not climb down. The last page is blank. I have never been so frightened by a blank page.

reviews.head: 'Reclaimed' (A Homecoming Memoir)
reviews.body: An inspiring account of dwarves returning to their fallen ancestral halls, dusting the furniture and evicting a lot of bats. The middle sags during the inventory chapters. The ending, a feast, is earned.

reviews.head: 'Rough' by Anonymous
reviews.body: A novel about a jeweler who cuts every gem in the fort the day before three moods arrive demanding rough ones. Thinly veiled; deeply felt. The villain is timing.

reviews.head: 'The World of {world}' (A Visitor's Guide)
reviews.body: A thorough guide to the world that has hosted all our forts. Strong on goblins, crooked horrors and refugee bands; weak on directions to taverns. The chapter on the most-claimed artifact is two words: 'still unworn'.

reviews.head: '{record}: The {record_fort} Story'
reviews.body: A sober history of how {record_fort} came to own {record}, told by the clerk who counted them. By chapter four he has stopped counting and started weeping. A cautionary tale for anyone with a work order.

reviews.head: 'Letters from {liaison}'
reviews.body: A collection of correspondence from {liaison}. Every letter begins 'there is much to share' and ends with a proposed import agreement. In between: weather, rings, more rings. Reads like a siege with stationery.

reviews.head: The Pump Ring Ensemble
reviews.body: Twelve pump operators performing in rhythm while the mist ring sprays the audience. The tempo never changes. The melody never arrives. The mood afterwards was extraordinary. Bring a cloak; the music is wet.

reviews.head: 'Ballad of the Meat Watch'
reviews.body: A sorrowful song, forty verses long, each describing a meal that did not include meat. The thirteenth verse is sung entirely by dogs. I cried. The dogs were very good.

reviews.head: 'Off Duty Blues' by the Militia Captain
reviews.body: A solo performance by our captain, accompanied by nine empty chairs. Mournful, slow, with a long silence where the chorus should be sung by the rest of the squad. Musically thin; emotionally a siege.

reviews.head: The Throne Choir
reviews.body: Over a hundred singers, each on a surplus throne, singing about armor stands. Acoustically impressive. Lyrically limited. The thrones creaked in harmony, which was the highlight.

reviews.head: 'There Is Much To Share' (Liaison Remix)
reviews.body: A single phrase, sung by the liaison, repeated for an hour over a drumbeat. I left humming it. I am still humming it. I have signed an import agreement and do not remember how.

reviews.head: 'Thirty Levels Down' (A Lament)
reviews.body: A grim, beautiful song for those lost in a Safety burrow. Each verse descends one level. By the end the singer is whispering. The audience was very quiet, and then very angry at the stairs.

reviews.head: 'March of {enemy}' (Performed by Prisoners)
reviews.body: A war song of {enemy}, sung by captured {enemy_race} raiders as part of their rehabilitation. Loud, tuneless and about us. The cell acoustics are excellent. The lyrics are not for children.

reviews.head: 'The Fey Carpenter'
reviews.body: A tragedy in three acts. A carpenter, gripped by a mood, dies of thirst beside a hundred and fifty rough gems. The gems are played by real gems, which stole the show and did not offer him a drink.

reviews.head: 'Waiting for the Loom Room'
reviews.body: A possessed weaver waits for a workshop that never frees up. Nothing happens, twice. Some called it pointless. Others, who have tried to get into the loom room, called it a documentary.

reviews.head: 'Production Order Violation!'
reviews.body: A courtroom farce in which the mayor charges everyone, then the furniture, then the audience. I was charged during the interval. The fine was a mug. It was a good mug. I miss it.

reviews.head: 'The Goblins Who Inherited a Fort'
reviews.body: A comedy imagining goblin occupiers trying to understand dwarven furniture. A goblin sitting on a barrel for an entire act, trying to work out the bung, is the funniest thing I have seen this year.

reviews.head: 'The Child Who Wanted Plant Cloth'
reviews.body: A short, sweet play about a young dwarf seized by a mood and the whole fort scrambling for fibre. The child actor delivered every line with terrifying focus. I now fear children.

reviews.head: 'The Great Rewind'
reviews.body: The cast performs Act One. Then the lights flicker and they perform Act One again, slightly differently. Then again. Daring, disorienting, and I still do not know how it ends. Neither do they.

reviews.head: 'The Last Days of {past_fort}'
reviews.body: A historical drama about {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}. The first act is a party. The second act is a ledger. The third act I will not spoil, except to say the barrels were full throughout.

reviews.head: 'Ode to the Last Rough Gem'
reviews.body: Short, passionate verses addressed to a single uncut gem, hidden from the jewelers for the day a mood demands it. The poet refused to say where it is hidden. Rightly so. Sincere and practical.

reviews.head: 'Haiku for the Hauler in the Pit'
reviews.body: Seventeen syllables: 'Haul it out, they said. / Throw it in, they also said. / I am in the pit.' I have thought about it every day since.

reviews.head: 'A Branch, a Miner, a Thirst'
reviews.body: A long poem told from the point of view of the tree. The tree is sorry. The tree also notes it never asked to be climbed. Morally complicated; botanically sound.

reviews.head: 'To Arms! (Arm, Singular)'
reviews.body: Rousing war verse urging the fort to arms. Unfortunately the fort's arms consist of one captain, off duty. The poem's call to battle was answered by a cat. Stirring, if under-attended.

reviews.head: 'Elegy for {past_fort}'
reviews.body: A gentle lament for an old fort, its barrels, its dogs and its long wait for meat. It lasted {past_fort_years}. The final stanza imagines its new tenants finally finding the meat. Unbearably sad.

reviews.head: Armor Stand Couture
reviews.body: A designer has dressed one armor stand, out of a surplus numbering in the thousands, in a full suit of iron. The rest attended the show in protest, wearing nothing. Striking.

reviews.head: The Mist Ring Look
reviews.body: Damp beards, slick hair and a cloak worn inside out to stay dry. This season everyone is wearing the mist ring whether they like it or not. Flattering on dwarves with curls; tragic on the rest.

reviews.head: The Seven Silk Scraps
reviews.body: A daring collection made entirely from seven silk scraps, the same seven that once hid a whole cloth shortage. The scraps are now socks. They hide nothing. Brave, small and very breezy.

reviews.head: Off-Duty Militia Wear
reviews.body: Slippers, a loose tunic and an unused helmet carried under one arm. The captain's look has been copied all over the fort. Comfortable, aspirational, and of no use in a siege.

reviews.head: {masterwright}'s New Line
reviews.body: Bold choices from {masterwright}, who insists every outfit include a hidden water skin, 'for the trees'. Practical, thoughtful, and slightly ominous. The cut is excellent.

reviews.head: The Meat Watch Tasting Menu
reviews.body: A recreation of a meatless founding feast: plump helmet, plump helmet, and a dish called 'The Memory of Meat', which is a plate. Historically faithful. I left hungry and a little haunted.

reviews.head: The Famine Platter
reviews.body: Seventeen leaves shared between ten diners. Very authentic. Conversation was tense. Someone counted the leaves aloud. A dwarf at the next table ate a candle. Nostalgia, at its most literal.

reviews.head: Lunch in the Safety Burrow
reviews.body: Quiet, deep and very private. Halfway through the soup we heard something on the stairs and moved the meal up twenty-nine levels. The soup was good. The stairs were better, for once.

reviews.head: Supper Beside the Cistern
reviews.body: Candlelight, still water, and a cup from the cistern itself, served with ceremony. After all the thirsty histories of our forts, a plentiful drink felt like a banquet. Five stars for wet.

reviews.head: The Tree-Top Café
reviews.body: A dining platform up a tree, with no ladder down. The view is lovely. The service is quick, because the waiter is very motivated to finish his shift and leave. Do not order the dry biscuits.

reviews.head: Dinner with {liaison}
reviews.body: The food was fine. I never finished it, because every bite was followed by 'there is much to share' and a proposal for imported cheese. Dessert was an import agreement. I did not sign. I did eat it.

reviews.head: The Off-Duty Bar
reviews.body: A tavern beside the barracks frequented entirely by the militia captain, who drinks alone in a room built for ten. Excellent service, because he is the only customer. Heartbreaking ambience.

reviews.head: The Refugee's Rest
reviews.body: A warm, cramped tavern popular with travellers driven from their towns by goblin armies. The stories are long, the soup is longer, and everyone has an opinion about goblins. Generous, if loud.

reviews.head: The Tavern with {drinks} Drinks
reviews.body: The cellars are bursting and the barmaid reminds every guest of every miner who died of thirst beside a full cellar. Nobody leaves thirsty here, by policy. One patron was carried home sober for violating it.

reviews.head: The Throne Room Pub
reviews.body: Bar stools replaced by surplus thrones from a runaway work order. Each patron rules their own small kingdom of ale. Disputes over borders are frequent. Majestic, uncomfortable, popular.

reviews.head: The {past_fort} Arms
reviews.body: A cellar tavern named for {past_fort}, decorated with its old barrels. Every barrel is within three steps of every chair, in tribute. Signs on every wall read 'DRINK.' A memorial and a menu. I obeyed.

reviews.head: The 148 Thrones of Quakefocus
reviews.body: A throne room with one hundred and forty-eight thrones and no monarch, beside 1,981 armor stands, also unemployed. Quakefocus built the most furniture per dwarf in history. I sat in eleven thrones. Overwhelming.

reviews.head: '1,994 Drinks: The Searabbeys Story'
reviews.body: The tale of Bomrek Enshalcatten, found dead of thirst while Searabbeys held 1,994 drinks. Three hundred pages asking how. The answer, on the last page, is 'stairs'. Devastating. Have a mug nearby.

reviews.head: 'The Claimants' Guide to The Amusing Duties'
reviews.body: A directory of all forty-eight figures who have claimed the famous greaves since Roughnessslaps. Each entry ends with 'did not wear them'. Excellent reference; terrible fashion advice.

reviews.head: 'The Goblins of Searabbeys'
reviews.body: The Torments of Hating, occupiers of Searabbeys, try to understand The Nuanced Hamlet. They put it on a different shelf. Then another. Two hours of goblins moving an artifact. I laughed until I wept.

reviews.head: 'Elegy for Searabbeys'
reviews.body: A gentle lament for our first fort, its two thousand barrels, its thirteen dogs and its long Meat Watch. The final stanza imagines The Torments of Hating finally finding the meat. Unbearably sad.

reviews.head: The Amusing Duties (Viewed Through Glass)
reviews.body: I went to Fieryaged to see the famous greaves. They are steel, they are fine, and forty-eight people have claimed them without once putting them on. Fashion's greatest unworn item.

reviews.head: The 1,994
reviews.body: A cellar tavern named after the Searabbeys drink count. Every barrel is within three steps of every chair. Signs on every wall read 'DRINK.' A memorial and a menu. I obeyed again.

world_news.head: GOBLINS AT {past_fort} STILL CANNOT OPEN BARRELS
world_news.body: The goblins now living in our old fort of {past_fort} are reported to be baffled by its barrels. Scouts say they have tried biting them, praying to them and stacking them into a throne. Not one has found the bung.

world_news.head: {enemy} REAFFIRM WAR, ASK HOW WE ARE
world_news.body: Envoys of {enemy} have restated their policy of war on {civ}. The letter ends, unusually, with 'hope the fort is well'. Scholars believe this was a threat. Our mayor has charged the letter with a production order violation.

world_news.head: {enemy} INSIST LATEST RAID WAS 'JUST A SKIRMISH'
world_news.body: A spokesman for {enemy} says recent fighting with {civ} was 'casual' and 'not the real war, which we are saving'. Analysts describe it as the most polite rivalry in {enemy_race} history.

world_news.head: GOBLIN ARMY DENIES BEING 'CRAZED'
world_news.body: A spokesgoblin for a war band that recently emptied three human towns says its fearsome name is 'an old family nickname' and 'only half accurate'. He would not say which half. He was holding three torches at the time.

world_news.head: WARLORD TOPS 'MOST REFUGEES CREATED' RANKING
world_news.body: A goblin warlord from {darkfort} has topped an unofficial ranking of leaders by number of towns emptied. His co-leader has demanded a recount, claiming at least half of the last town left because of her.

world_news.head: {darkfort} SENDS AMBASSADOR TO STUDY 'FORT OCCUPYING'
world_news.body: The goblins of {darkfort} have sent a delegation to learn how goblins elsewhere managed to occupy an entire dwarven fort. The answer, reportedly, was 'it was mostly barrels and nobody stopped us'.

world_news.head: {darkfort} ASKS {darkfort2} TO 'KEEP IT DOWN'
world_news.body: A noise complaint has been lodged between the dark fortresses of {darkfort} and {darkfort2}. The complaint concerns drumming. The drumming concerns the complaint. Both sides are said to be enjoying it enormously.

world_news.head: RECLAIMERS FINISH DUSTING ANCESTRAL HALLS
world_news.body: A dwarven band has declared the reclamation of a fallen fortress near {hillock} complete after a final sweep of the dining hall. Its leader reports finding seventeen goblin skulls, four lost socks and one perfectly good mug.

world_news.head: RECLAMATION 'SLOWER THAN WE'D LIKE'
world_news.body: A group of dwarves reclaiming a lost fort near {hillock} admits progress is 'slower than we'd like, owing to the ghosts'. They have requested a shipment of slabs, a priest and a group with a less unlucky name.

world_news.head: {monarch} STILL HAS ONE THRONE, COURT INSISTS
world_news.body: The court of {civ} has denied receiving any of the surplus thrones from our forts' runaway work orders. '{monarch} has a throne,' said a spokesdwarf. 'One. It is sufficient.' Several forts have offered to send a few, just in case.

world_news.head: DIPLOMAT 'NOT THE LIAISON', HE STRESSES
world_news.body: Our civilization's diplomat has issued a statement clarifying that he and {liaison} are different dwarves. 'I do not say there is much to share,' he said. 'I share it.' He then shared a treaty, which was long.

world_news.head: CAPITAL IMPRESSED BY OUR 'ARMOR STAND HERITAGE'
world_news.body: Visitors from the capital of {civ} have described our forts' armor stand surpluses as 'a national treasure, sort of'. A museum has been proposed. It would require two thousand plinths, which are, the curators note, very nearly armor stands.

world_news.head: {liaison} FILES REPORT: 'MUCH WAS SHARED'
world_news.body: {liaison}'s latest report to the capital runs to forty pages and contains the phrase 'there is much to share' on each one. The final page recommends an import agreement. The capital has recommended a shorter report.

world_news.head: FRIENDLY NATIONS SEND GREETINGS; ENEMIES SEND ARMIES
world_news.body: {civ} received season's greetings from every group it is at peace with this {season}. Those it is at war with sent armies instead, which officials have chosen to interpret as a very large card.

world_news.head: {liaison} OFFERS RINGS AT DOUBLE, CALLS IT 'GENEROUS'
world_news.body: {liaison} has defended a request for rings at twice their value. 'That is what friendship costs,' he said. Jewelers across the realm have responded by inventing a new ring, worth exactly half as much, for liaisons.

world_news.head: HUMANS REFUSE TO RETURN OCCUPIED TOWN
world_news.body: Human councillors who occupied a town near {town} have rejected calls to give it back. 'We've just finished the decorating,' a councillor said. The evicted residents say the decorating was already there.

world_news.head: {town} BAKERS SEND CAKES TO {civ}
world_news.body: The humans of {town} have sent a gift of cakes to {civ}. The cakes were fair. The dwarves who received them were suspicious, ate them anyway, and have since requested more, in the name of diplomacy.

world_news.head: EVICTED GROUP CHANGES LEADER, ADDRESS
world_news.body: A band evicted from its town by goblins has announced a new leader and a new home near {town2}. They thank their former neighbours for 'a brief but well-stocked stay' and request that mail be sent somewhere without goblins.

world_news.head: ELVES DEMAND RETURN OF ABDUCTED POET
world_news.body: The elves of {retreat} have issued a fourth demand for the return of a poet abducted by goblins. The demand was written on a leaf. The goblins, who cannot read leaves, have used it to wrap a sandwich.

world_news.head: {retreat} HOLDS TREE-FRIENDLY VIGIL
world_news.body: Elves at {retreat} held a candle-free, tree-friendly vigil for a kinsman abducted last year. Attendees sat in total darkness for nine hours. Many say they found it peaceful. Several are still sitting there.

world_news.head: ELVES 'CONCERNED' BY DWARVEN WINDMILLS
world_news.body: The elves of {retreat} have written to complain that dwarven windmills are 'spinning wood in an aggressive manner'. We have replied that the windmills are merely enthusiastic, and that their complaint was written on wood.

world_news.head: {retreat} BANS THE WORD 'LUMBER'
world_news.body: The council of {retreat} has made the word 'lumber' illegal. Offenders will be sentenced to hugging a tree for one season. Our correspondent said 'lumber' by accident and is now on good terms with an oak.

world_news.head: CROOKED HORROR NEAR {town} 'JUST WANTS QUIET'
world_news.body: Residents near {town} report that a crooked horror in the hills has become restless again. A local sage claims the beast 'only wants quiet'. Residents have offered it quiet, firmly, from very far away.

world_news.head: FAMOUS GREAVES GAIN NEW CLAIMANT
world_news.body: A fresh claim has been lodged on a pair of famous lost greaves. The new claimant, like the forty-odd before him, has not yet travelled to where they lie, but says he 'feels very strongly about it'.

world_news.head: {town} UNVEILS PLAQUE: 'ARTIFACT LOST HERE'
world_news.body: The townsfolk of {town} have installed a plaque marking where a legendary artifact was lost long ago. It is already the most visited spot in town. Three visitors have claimed the plaque.

world_news.head: RAIDED TOWN ASKS GOBLINS TO 'PICK ONE ARMY'
world_news.body: {town2}, raided by two goblin armies in one year, has begun rebuilding. The mayor has written to both armies requesting that they 'decide between yourselves who is attacking us' to cut down on paperwork.

world_news.head: CARAVANS DEMAND 'NO TREES' CLAUSE
world_news.body: Merchants travelling to dwarven forts have asked for a guarantee that no dwarf will be found stuck in a tree near the depot. The guild says this is 'a reasonable request, based on the history of the region'.

world_news.head: MARKET FOR ARMOR STANDS COLLAPSES
world_news.body: Prices for armor stands have fallen to an all-time low after records revealed one dwarven fort alone produced nearly two thousand. Traders in {town} are offering three armor stands for one mug, and are still not getting takers.

world_news.head: ROUGH GEMS FETCH RECORD PRICES
world_news.body: Rough, uncut gems are now the most sought-after goods among dwarven forts, as craftsdwarfs fear a mood demanding one the day after the last is cut. Some forts now keep a 'mood reserve' in a vault with guards.

world_news.head: PLANT CLOTH SHORTAGE BLAMED ON CHILDREN
world_news.body: Weavers report a sudden shortage of plant cloth after a famous strange mood in which a dwarven child demanded some. 'Every child now wants a mood,' a weaver said. 'Every child now asks for cloth.'

world_news.head: {record_fort}'S {record} STILL ON THE MARKET
world_news.body: Traders in {town} report that the famous stock of {record_fort}, namely {record}, is still being offered at bargain prices. Buyers are scarce. 'Everybody knows what happened,' one merchant said. 'Nobody wants to be next.'

world_news.head: WATER NOW CHEAPER THAN ALE IN {town}
world_news.body: A drought of nothing at all has made water cheaper than ale in {town} for the first time. Dwarven visitors have reacted with deep suspicion and continue drinking ale, on principle and out of habit.

world_news.head: INSURERS REFUSE TO COVER 'SAFETY' BURROWS
world_news.body: A guild of insurers has declined to cover any dwarven room named 'Safety'. 'It's always the ones called Safety,' a spokesman said. Forts are advised to call them 'Moderately Dangerous Room' to keep premiums down.

world_news.head: REFUSE HAULING DECLARED 'MOST HAZARDOUS JOB'
world_news.body: A survey of dwarven labour has ranked refuse hauling above mining, smelting and fighting forgotten beasts as the most dangerous job in the realm, chiefly because of garbage pits. The haulers' guild is negotiating for helmets.

world_news.head: {fort} DRINK STOCKS ENVIED ACROSS REALM
world_news.body: Merchants report that {fort}'s {drinks} drinks are the talk of the region. 'Not that they'll drink them,' a merchant added. We consider this unkind, and we are keeping a close eye on the stairs.

world_news.head: SCHOLARS CANNOT EXPLAIN 'THIRST PARADOX'
world_news.body: A college of dwarven scholars has spent a year studying why dwarves die of thirst surrounded by drink. Their final report concludes 'the stairs, probably, or a tree'. Their research was funded by a brewery, which is now nervous.

world_news.head: SCHOLARS CONFIRM: GEMS NOT A DRINK
world_news.body: After a carpenter died of thirst beside a pile of rough gems, scholars in {town} tested whether gems could be consumed as liquid. Results: they cannot. Funding has been requested for a follow-up on thrones.

world_news.head: SAGES STUDY 'WORLD BLINK' EVENT
world_news.body: Sages report that the whole world briefly stopped and restarted this {season}. Nobody can agree on what happened, because nobody can agree on whether it happened. Dwarves call it a Great Rewind; elves call it a nap.

world_news.head: TREES 'NOT DESIGNED FOR MINERS', ARBORISTS SAY
world_news.body: Arborists from {retreat} have published findings that trees are poorly suited to dwarven use, especially as a place to get stuck. They recommend that miners 'look at the tree, not climb it'. Miners say they will look into it.

world_news.head: {weather} OVER {darkfort}
world_news.body: It is {weather} over {darkfort} this week, though residents note the sky there is always dark and the weather hard to see. A crooked horror was reportedly seen enjoying it.

world_news.head: PERPETUAL DRIZZLE REPORTED AT {fort}
world_news.body: Foreign visitors to {fort} describe the region as 'damp' after walking through a ring of misting pumps by accident. Local weather is in fact fine. The pumps are just very enthusiastic.

world_news.head: PLANT GATHERERS SPOTTED IN RAIN ACROSS MAP
world_news.body: Travellers report dwarves wandering every corner of the region in the rain, carrying single strawberries home from impossible distances. The Overseer has confirmed this is 'part of the plan'. Travellers have not been told the plan.

world_news.head: GHOSTS OF {past_fort} 'STILL WATCHING FOR MEAT'
world_news.body: Travellers passing {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}, report ghostly dwarves in the halls at night, pointing at empty plates and whispering 'meat?'. Offerings of bones have not satisfied them. They want it cooked.

world_news.head: {artifact} SAID TO BE ENVIED IN {darkfort2}
world_news.body: Rumour reaches us that the goblins of {darkfort2} have heard of {artifact} and are 'very interested'. Readers will remember what happens to artifacts left in fallen forts. Readers are asked to keep {artifact} indoors.

world_news.head: MILITIA CAPTAIN SEEN ON DUTY, BRIEFLY
world_news.body: Unconfirmed reports say the captain of a certain dwarven militia was seen in uniform, at attention, for nearly a minute. Witnesses add that he then looked around, saw nobody else, and went back off duty.

world_news.head: OVERSEER ACCUSED OF 'EXCESSIVE SMOOTHING'
world_news.body: A complaint from neighbouring forts accuses the Overseer of smoothing 'a frankly unreasonable number of walls'. The Overseer has replied that walls are 'improved by smoothing', and has queued smoothing for the complaint.

world_news.head: {liaison} SEEN SIGNING OWN IMPORT AGREEMENT
world_news.body: {liaison} was reportedly seen proposing an import agreement to himself in a mirror, then accepting it. 'There was much to share,' he said later. Officials are reviewing every agreement he has ever signed.

world_news.head: MAYOR CHARGES SELF WITH ORDER VIOLATION
world_news.body: In a remarkable act of fairness, a dwarven mayor has charged himself with failing to meet his own mandate. He found himself guilty, fined himself one mug and drank it as punishment. Observers called the trial 'swift and thirsty'.

world_news.head: NEW MAP SHOWS EVERY TREE A MINER HAS CLIMBED
world_news.body: Cartographers have published a map of {world} marking every tree a dwarf has climbed and failed to get down. It is a very small map. It is mostly one tree. The tree has asked to be removed.

world_news.head: {hillock} REDRAWN TO AVOID GOBLINS
world_news.body: Mapmakers have moved {hillock} two days' walk on their charts, hoping goblin armies use the same maps. The dwarves of {hillock} have not moved and are said to be 'hoping it works'.

world_news.head: OUR FORTS IN {world}: A RETROSPECTIVE
world_news.body: Historians mark the line of dwarven forts in {world}, from {past_fort}, which lasted {past_fort_years}, to {fort} today, each inheriting the ghosts, rumours and furniture of the last. 'Each one learns something,' one said. 'Not much.'

world_news.head: {record}: HOW DID IT HAPPEN?
world_news.body: A new study of {record_fort} asks how a single fort accumulated {record}. The answer, after two hundred pages, is 'one work order, never cancelled'. The study recommends checking your work orders. Please check your work orders.

world_news.head: ELVES STAGE 'TRAGEDY OF THE TREE-BOUND MINER'
world_news.body: A troupe at {retreat} has premiered a play about a dwarf who climbed a tree and never came down. In their version, the tree is the hero. Dwarven audiences walked out at intermission and climbed nothing on the way home.

world_news.head: GOBLIN POET WRITES ODE TO 'ALL THOSE BARRELS'
world_news.body: A goblin poet stationed in a captured dwarven fort has published a collection about its stores. Highlights include 'Barrel', 'Another Barrel' and 'Why Won't It Open'. Critics in {darkfort} called it 'raw'.

world_news.head: HUMANS OF {town} BUILD ONE ARMOR STAND, CALL IT ART
world_news.body: Humans in {town} have built a single armor stand and placed it in the town square as public art. Dwarven visitors were unimpressed. 'Come back when you have two thousand,' one said, before realising this was not a boast.

world_news.head: HUMANS ASK WHY DWARVES DIE NEAR BARRELS
world_news.body: Your correspondent in {town} is regularly asked why dwarves are famous for dying of thirst in well-stocked forts. I have explained the stairs, the trees and the orders. They nod slowly. They do not understand. Neither, quite, do I.

world_news.head: TOWN GUARD ADMIRES OUR MILITIA'S 'EFFICIENCY'
world_news.body: The captain of the guard in {town} has praised our militia for keeping costs so low. I did not tell him it is one dwarf. I did not tell him the dwarf is off duty. I let {town} have its admiration, and bought him a drink.

world_news.head: {town2} BAKERS HEAR OF 'FAMINE, DAY 32'
world_news.body: Bakers in {town2} were horrified to learn of a starving dwarven founding and have sent a sack of bread 'for the history'. I have explained that the famine was some years ago. They have sent a second sack, for the present.

world_news.head: {past_fort} LISTED: 'BARRELS INCLUDED'
world_news.body: A property notice describes {past_fort} as 'well-stocked, spacious, full of character', and mentions in small print that it {past_fort_fate}. Viewing is by appointment, and possibly by siege.

world_news.head: OLD FORT RUINS 'FULLY FURNISHED'
world_news.body: Agents describe a ruined dwarven fort near {hillock} as 'fully furnished, heavily furnished, possibly over-furnished', with over a hundred thrones and two thousand armor stands in the asking price. Smoothing incomplete.

world_news.head: EVERY FORT IN REALM SEEKS SHERIFF
world_news.body: Forts across {world} report the same vacancies: sheriff, hammerer, dungeon master, chief medical dwarf. Applicants are encouraged to apply anywhere. No experience needed. No applicants yet.

world_news.head: PUMP RINGS SPREAD AS 'HAPPINESS INFRASTRUCTURE'
world_news.body: Engineers in {hillock} have begun building rings of misting pumps, reporting a sharp rise in cheerful moods and damp beards. One fort has built a mist ring inside its tavern. Nobody is sure which drink is which.

world_news.head: GARBAGE PIT REFORM PROPOSED
world_news.body: Engineers have proposed a radical new refuse pit: one where nobody is asked to haul anything out while others are throwing things in. The proposal has been called 'visionary'. Several forts have asked for a diagram.

world_news.head: MYSTERIOUS LIGHTS OVER {darkfort2}
world_news.body: Travellers report flickering lights above {darkfort2} each night. Some say it is a goblin festival. Some say it is a goblin argument. Both, our night desk notes, involve torches.

world_news.head: FORGOTTEN BEAST SEEN 'USING STAIRS RESPONSIBLY'
world_news.body: A forgotten beast was reportedly seen using a staircase one step at a time 'like a citizen'. Dwarves who survived a similar visit to a Safety burrow have asked that this not be presented as good news.

world_news.head: ACADEMY OFFERS COURSE: 'CANCELLING WORK ORDERS'
world_news.body: A dwarven academy in {hillock} has launched a course teaching overseers to cancel work orders. Lesson one is finding the order. Lesson two is admitting how many armor stands it already made. Enrolment is one.

world_news.head: HISTORIANS DEBATE: WAS {past_fort} 'HAPPY'?
world_news.body: Scholars disagree on whether {past_fort} was happy. One side cites its barrels. The other side cites its fate: it {past_fort_fate}. A third side has gone to the tavern and is citing nothing.

world_news.head: GOBLINS AT SEARABBEYS STILL CANNOT FIND THE MEAT
world_news.body: The Torments of Hating, who occupy Searabbeys, report that the fort's famous two thousand barrels are 'all drink, no food'. Historians note the dwarves had the same complaint. The Nuanced Hamlet remains on its shelf.

world_news.head: VICE OF FINS CLAIMS IT HAS NO FINS
world_news.body: Uslôx Ulutodan, leader of The Vice of Fins, has dismissed rumours that his army is part fish. 'It is a vice,' he said. Survivors of the Padtufted raid say they did see at least one fin, but it may have been a hat.

world_news.head: CHASTE CUDGEL'S TAMETOMB 'DUSTED AT LAST'
world_news.body: Bomrek Thimshursåkzul of The Chaste Cudgel reports that Tametomb is fully reclaimed. Meanwhile The Oily Boots continue to slide toward Scaldedarch, requesting sand and a less slippery name.

world_news.head: AMUSING DUTIES GAINS 49TH CLAIMANT
world_news.body: A fresh claim has been lodged on The Amusing Duties, the steel greaves lost at Roughnessslaps in year 68 and now at Fieryaged. The new claimant, like the forty-eight before, has not yet travelled to Fieryaged.

world_news.head: CLASPEDSERPENT 'MISSES' QUAKEFOCUS
world_news.body: The silver mace Claspedserpent is said to rattle on its pedestal at Quakefocus every year on the anniversary of the 1,981st armor stand. Experts suggest it is a draft. Romantics suggest it is grief.

world_news.head: NOBLEDESSERT DEMANDS RETURN OF MAME AYATHEMIYI
world_news.body: The elves of Nobledessert, joined by Keeperglossed in the matter of Imara Sidayanithe, have issued a joint demand for their abducted kin. It was written on a leaf. Goblins have used it to wrap a sandwich.

world_news.head: GROOVED COUNCIL KEEPS JACKALDEFENSE
world_news.body: The humans of The Grooved Council say they will not return Jackaldefense to The Distinct Dungeon. 'We've just finished the grooves,' a councillor said. The jackals were not consulted.

world_news.head: PADTUFTED ASKS GOBLINS TO PICK ONE ARMY
world_news.body: Padtufted, raided by both The Crazed Hex and The Vice of Fins, has written to both requesting they 'decide between yourselves who is attacking us'. Ngumrash Ensebrab replied 'both'.

travel.head: A WEEKEND AT {past_fort}
travel.body: Our reviewer visited {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}. The halls are grand, the barrels plentiful, the ghosts chatty. Do not ask the ghosts about meat. Do not drink from the barrels. Do not stay the night, whatever the ghosts suggest.

travel.head: {past_fort}: A GUIDED TOUR FOR THE BRAVE
travel.body: The guide to {past_fort} opens every tour with 'it lasted {past_fort_years}', then pauses for effect. Highlights include the old still, the long walk to it, and a staircase the guide refuses to discuss. Bring water. Obviously.

travel.head: SEE {record} AT {record_fort}!
travel.body: Tourists flock to {record_fort} to gawp at its famous {record}. Our reviewer counted for an hour before losing his place. The gift shop sells one, as a souvenir. It is the only one anyone has ever bought.

travel.head: THE {civ} CAPITAL ON A BUDGET
travel.body: The capital of {civ} is grand, crowded and expensive. Our reviewer suggests the free attractions: watching {monarch}'s single throne from across the hall, and listening to petitioners. Avoid the liaison's office unless you want to sign something.

travel.head: TRAVELLING WITH {liaison}
travel.body: Our reviewer shared a wagon with {liaison} for six days. We learned there is much to share. We learned it again each morning. By day four we had agreed to an import of cheese. By day six we were importing it ourselves.

travel.head: NOT RECOMMENDED: {enemy} TERRITORY
travel.body: {enemy} have opened their borders to visitors, in the sense that they have opened them at us with spears. Our reviewer saw the scenery briefly, at speed, while leaving. Zero stars. Lovely hills, though.

travel.head: {town}: A HUMAN TOWN WITH TREES (CAREFUL)
travel.body: {town} has a charming square, a good inn and a great many trees, all of which our reviewer declined to climb. The humans found this odd. We explained the history. They have since put up little signs: 'NOT FOR MINERS'.

travel.head: {town2}: REFUGEE CAPITAL OF THE REGION
travel.body: {town2} has taken in refugees from three goblin raids and is now the busiest town for weeks around. Every inn is full, every story is grim, and every soup is generous. Visit for the company; leave before the goblins check the address.

travel.head: DARK TOURISM: {darkfort}
travel.body: A goblin tour of {darkfort} includes the spear gallery, the prisoner gallery and the gallery of spears taken from prisoners. The tour guide was charming and would not let our reviewer leave for three days. Five stars for hospitality, one for exit.

travel.head: {darkfort2}: THE TOWER IS THE ATTRACTION
travel.body: {darkfort2} has one tall tower, built in what goblins consider a fun style. Visitors may climb it. Visitors may not come down until they have heard every war song. There are forty war songs.

travel.head: {retreat}: LEAVE THE AXE AT HOME
travel.body: Elves at {retreat} were welcoming once they had searched our reviewer's pack for wood. They found a pencil. The pencil was given a funeral. Our reviewer was given a bowl of leaves and told to be grateful. He was, eventually.

travel.head: {retreat} FOREST WALKS
travel.body: The forest walks at {retreat} are long, green and conducted at elf pace, which is to say one step per century. Our reviewer finished the short loop in under a season and was praised for his 'urgency'.

travel.head: {hillock}: A DWARF HAMLET THAT GETS IT
travel.body: {hillock} has a still beside every bed and a ladder at every tree. No room is called 'Safety'. Our reviewer wept with recognition and asked to stay. He was put to work smoothing, so he left.

travel.head: {hillock}'S FAMOUS GARBAGE POLICY
travel.body: {hillock} has a famous rule: nobody hauls refuse out of the pit while anyone is throwing it in. Visitors come from all over to see it. It is a sign. It works. Our reviewer took a rubbing of the sign to bring home.

travel.head: THE ROAD TO {town}: MIND THE GOBLINS
travel.body: The road from {fort} to {town} is pleasant, dry and lined with burned wagons. Travellers are advised to go in groups, carry water and ignore anyone offering a 'shortcut through the woods'. The shortcut leads to {darkfort}.

travel.head: A CARAVAN RIDE TO {town2}
travel.body: Our reviewer joined a caravan to {town2}. The wagons were slow, the oxen proud and the merchants spent the trip complaining about dwarven depots. 'Why underground?' they asked every hour. We told them the whole history. They stopped asking.

travel.head: CAMPING IN {world}: A GUIDE
travel.body: Pitch your tent away from trees, rivers, caverns, goblins, elves, carp and crooked horrors. Our reviewer did this successfully and camped in the middle of a bare field. He reports it was 'very safe and the worst night of my life'.

travel.head: VISITING A FORT CALLED 'SAFETY'
travel.body: Our reviewer visited a dwarven settlement whose founders had named it, optimistically, Safety. Its burrows, its stairs and its trees were all safe on the day of the visit. Our reviewer left before the day ended, on principle.

travel.head: THE CAVERN TOUR, FIRST LAYER
travel.body: Mushroom trees, glowing moss and the occasional forgotten beast, which the guide described as 'part of the experience'. Our reviewer enjoyed the moss, avoided the experience and returned by a different staircase out of sheer superstition.

travel.head: A SPA WEEK IN A MIST RING
travel.body: Some forts build rings of misting pumps purely for joy, and our reviewer spent a week in one. Skin: glowing. Beard: permanently damp. Mood: radiant. He now finds dry rooms suspicious and has asked to be sprinkled before meetings.

travel.head: THE CATACOMB WALK
travel.body: Every dwarven fort has catacombs, and every dwarven fort is proud of its catacombs. Our reviewer took the tour at {fort}. Slabs, niches, a ghost with opinions about the decor. The ghost was right about the decor.

travel.head: THE EXECUTION TOWER (EXTERIOR ONLY)
travel.body: Visitors to {fort} are encouraged to admire the execution tower from the outside. The architecture is fine. The view is reported to be excellent. Nobody on our staff has confirmed this personally, by choice.

travel.head: THE ARMOR STAND MUSEUM, ANY FORT
travel.body: Most dwarven forts with an Overseer have, somewhere, an armor stand museum: a hall of furniture made by a work order nobody cancelled. Entry free. Exit eventually. Our reviewer touched one stand for luck. It fell over. Bad luck.

travel.head: THE THRONE HALL TOUR
travel.body: Somewhere in every ambitious fort is a hall of surplus thrones. Visitors may sit in as many as they like. Our reviewer managed thirty before feeling dangerously regal and had to lie down in a normal bed.

travel.head: HIKING TO THE FORT ON THE HILL
travel.body: Our reviewer hiked from {hillock} toward a ruined fortress said to be full of barrels. He got lost, ran out of water and was found three days later, sitting beside a barrel. Readers will appreciate the irony. He did not, at the time.

travel.head: A HUMAN MARKET IN {town}
travel.body: The market at {town} sells everything except what dwarves need. Our reviewer asked for rough gems and was offered cut ones. He asked for plant cloth and was offered silk. He came home with a hat. It is a good hat.

travel.head: {town} INN: BEDS, BREAD AND BAD STAIRS
travel.body: The inn at {town} is warm and friendly, with a staircase so steep our reviewer suspects dwarven design. He slept downstairs. He ate downstairs. He did not go upstairs. 'You never know what is coming up,' he said, darkly.

travel.head: ELF TEA AT {retreat}
travel.body: Tea at {retreat} is brewed for a full season and served in a leaf. It tastes of patience. Our reviewer finished his cup in eleven seconds and was asked if he was 'alright'. He was not. He wanted ale.

travel.head: {darkfort}: THE GOBLIN BAKE-OFF
travel.body: {darkfort} hosts an annual baking contest. Entries this year included bread, spear-bread and bread with a prisoner's name iced on it. Our reviewer was a judge. He declined to taste the third. He was not invited back, which he counts as a win.

travel.head: THE OLD TRADE ROAD
travel.body: The old trade road across {world} passes three ruined dwarven forts, two goblin towers and one surprisingly good inn. Our reviewer recommends the inn and very little else. Pack water; history says you will need it.

travel.head: ON FOOT FROM {hillock} TO {town}
travel.body: A gentle week's walk, our reviewer reports, through fields, woods and the occasional refugee camp. Everyone he met had fled a goblin army. Everyone shared their bread. He returned fatter and sadder, and with three new recipes.

travel.head: STAYING WITH REFUGEES NEAR {town2}
travel.body: Refugees camped near {town2} have opened their tents to travellers. The food is simple, the stories are long and everyone knows the name of the goblin general who chased them out. Our reviewer did too, by the end. He would rather not.

travel.head: A DIPLOMATIC JOURNEY
travel.body: Our reviewer accompanied a diplomat of {civ} on a tour of friendly nations. Every capital served cake. Every speech mentioned peace. Every meeting ended with an import agreement. He returned with a new appreciation for staying home.

travel.head: THE TREE OF REGRETS
travel.body: Locals near {hillock} point visitors to a single tall tree where, they say, a miner once climbed and could not climb down. Tourists photograph themselves next to it, never in it. The tree has become quite vain about the attention.

travel.head: THE TOWN THAT CHANGED HANDS
travel.body: Our reviewer visited a town near {town} recently taken by a human council. The new owners have changed the signs, the taxes and the name of the inn. The potholes remain loyal to the old regime.

travel.head: BEACH HOLIDAY? NO
travel.body: A reader asked if we would review a beach. Our reviewer went to the nearest shore, saw the carp, and came straight back. 'Every dwarf knows,' he wrote, in a short and shaky report. He has not been near water since, except to drink it, carefully.

travel.head: TRAVELLER'S NOTE: WATCH FOR CROOKED HORRORS
travel.body: Several regions of {world} are home to crooked horrors, enormous beasts with poor manners and good appetites. Travellers should consult locals, carry no food and walk quietly. Our reviewer walked so quietly he got lost. It was worth it.

travel.head: GLAMPING IN THE SAFETY BURROW
travel.body: A fort has begun renting out its deepest burrow to tourists as 'the safest stay in the region'. Our reviewer spent a night there. Nothing came up the stairs. He spent the whole night watching the stairs anyway. He calls it 'restful, technically'.

travel.head: THE SEARABBEYS HERITAGE WALK
travel.body: Searabbeys, our first fort, is occupied by The Torments of Hating, who have opened it for tours. Highlights: the 800 loose stones, the 1,994-drink cellar, The Nuanced Hamlet on its shelf. Do not mention the meat. The goblins are sensitive.

travel.head: QUAKEFOCUS: FURNITURE CAPITAL OF THE PLANES
travel.body: Quakefocus offers the world's largest collection of armor stands (1,981) and thrones (148), plus four hospitals, two once staffed. Claspedserpent is on display. The smoothing is still not finished. Allow a week.

travel.head: FIERYAGED: SEE THE AMUSING DUTIES
travel.body: The steel greaves lost at Roughnessslaps in year 68 now rest at Fieryaged. Visitors may view them and, for a small fee, register as claimant forty-nine. Nobody may wear them. Nobody has ever wanted to.

travel.head: TAMETOMB, NEWLY RECLAIMED
travel.body: The Chaste Cudgel's Tametomb is open to visitors. Bomrek Thimshursåkzul greets each one personally and shows them the dusting. A lovely hall, a little haunted, with a dining room that has seen goblins and survived.

travel.head: SHADYGHOSTS: DON'T
travel.body: Shadyghosts is home to the crooked horror Omo Fewethauyira. It is also home to some excellent views, which the locals describe at length from very far away. Our reviewer viewed them from the next valley. Recommended distance: further.

travel.head: TOEEMBRACE: FAIR CAKES, FAIR PRICES
travel.body: The Fair Cakes of Toeembrace bake the best cakes in the region and sell them at reasonable prices. The name of the town remains unexplained. Our reviewer asked about the toes. He was given a cake instead. He accepted the trade.

travel.head: A NIGHT AT THE DEPOT
travel.body: Our reviewer slept at the trade depot of {fort} to experience the caravan life. He was woken by merchants, then by an elf, then by the liaison, who had much to share. Breakfast was an import agreement. Two stars, both for the oxen.

travel.head: {hillock} HOT SPRINGS (A CISTERN)
travel.body: {hillock} advertises 'hot springs'. They are a cistern under the tavern, gently warmed by the kitchens. Our reviewer soaked for an hour and drank some for safety's sake. Nobody stopped him. Nobody ever stops a dwarf near water.

travel.head: THE WINDMILL FIELDS OF {world}
travel.body: Across {world}, dwarven windmills turn on hilltops for reasons the dwarves cannot fully explain. Our reviewer toured six. Each mechanic gave a different answer. The windmills themselves gave none, and kept turning.

sports.head: THIRST PARADOX RELAY ENDS IN FARCE
sports.body: Teams were asked to carry a full mug from the cellar to a thirsty dwarf two levels up. All six teams drank the mug on the way. The thirsty dwarf was eventually carried to the cellar instead, which judges ruled 'within the spirit of the event'.

sports.head: TREE-CLIMBING BANNED AFTER ONE ATTEMPT
sports.body: The fort's first tree-climbing contest was suspended after the only competitor reached the top branch and then asked, quietly, how one gets down. The league has replaced the event with 'looking at trees', which has a perfect safety record.

sports.head: ARMOR STAND SLALOM DRAWS RECORD FIELD
sports.body: Runners wove through two thousand armor stands in the fort's surplus gallery. The course record was set by a cat. The dwarven winner finished in a respectable time and knocked over only four hundred stands, which the Overseer immediately ordered replaced.

sports.head: MILITIA WINS SQUAD DRILL, UNOPPOSED
sports.body: Our militia has won the inter-squad drill competition for the fifth year running, being the only squad. The captain performed all ten positions himself, in sequence, and was awarded a medal by himself. He then went off duty to celebrate.

sports.head: THRONE-SITTING MARATHON CALLED OFF
sports.body: The throne-sitting marathon was abandoned after competitors could not agree which of the many surplus thrones counted as 'the' throne. Several moved between thrones every hour. The judges ruled that everyone was king and nobody won.

sports.head: SMOOTHING SPRINT: THREE ENTRANTS, SIXTEEN THOUSAND WALLS
sports.body: The smoothing sprint pitted three smoothers against the full job queue. Day one: four walls. Day thirty: sixty walls. The organisers have declared the event 'ongoing' and moved the medal ceremony to a later generation.

sports.head: GARBAGE PIT TUG-OF-WAR ENDS BADLY
sports.body: One team pulled refuse out of the pit. The other team threw it back in. Neither team realised they were competing. Medical staff report three injuries and one very confused goat. The event will not be repeated.

sports.head: SAFETY BURROW HIDE-AND-SEEK CANCELLED
sports.body: The annual hide-and-seek was cancelled after organisers realised the best hiding place was the Safety burrow, thirty levels down, and that a forgotten beast was 'it'. Players have been asked to hide in the tavern, where nobody seeks.

sports.head: GEM-HIDING CHAMPIONSHIP A TIE
sports.body: Jewelers and crafters competed to hide one rough gem from each other before the next strange mood. The jewelers found and cut every hidden gem within a day. The crafters responded by hiding the jewelers. The judges declared a tie.

sports.head: MAYOR'S CUP GOES TO 'PRODUCTION ORDER' TEAM
sports.body: The Mayor's Cup was awarded to the team that fulfilled the most mandates. It was the only team that bothered. The rest were charged with production order violations during the medal ceremony, which they described as 'fair, honestly'.

sports.head: PLANT-GATHERING CROSS-COUNTRY: EVERYONE LOST
sports.body: Runners were sent to gather plants from every edge of the map in the rain, by order of the Overseer. Nine returned with a strawberry each. Three returned with a cold. One is still out there and has been listed as 'still competing'.

sports.head: MIST RING DANCE-OFF A DAMP SUCCESS
sports.body: Competitors danced in the spray of a ring of misting pumps until they slipped. The last dwarf standing was a miner with exceptionally grippy boots. Everyone left happier, wetter and in need of a towel. The pumps were not judged.

sports.head: REFUSE-HAULING RELAY GETS HELMETS
sports.body: After past tragedies, the refuse-hauling relay now requires helmets, gloves and a spotter at the top of the pit shouting 'STOP THROWING'. Times are slower. Survival rates are excellent. Spectators described it as 'boring in a good way'.

sports.head: CHILD WINS CRAFTING CONTEST IN A MOOD
sports.body: A dwarven child seized by a strange mood entered the open crafting contest and produced a masterpiece out of plant cloth in a single afternoon. Adult entrants have lodged a protest, citing 'divine assistance'. The protest was ignored.

sports.head: WINDMILL-WATCHING LEAGUE: NO RESULT
sports.body: Teams were asked to explain what the windmill does. No team could. The match was declared a draw after nine hours of watching the windmill turn. Several spectators described it as 'the most relaxing sport we have'.

sports.head: LIAISON CHALLENGE: WHO CAN SAY 'NO' FIRST?
sports.body: Contestants sat across from the visiting liaison and tried to refuse an import agreement before he said 'there is much to share'. Nobody managed it. Six contestants signed something. One is now importing turnips. The trophy was imported.

sports.head: CATACOMB QUIET-WALKING EVENT
sports.body: Competitors walked the length of the catacombs without disturbing the dead. Two finished. One woke a ghost, who followed him to the tavern and has opinions about his technique. The ghost has since been made a judge.

sports.head: HOSPITAL DASH: FIND THE DOCTOR
sports.body: Runners raced through four hospitals to find the one with a doctor. Most runners reached hospitals with beds, splints and buckets but no doctor. The winner found the doctor in the tavern. The doctor was also in the race and came second.

sports.head: BURROW DRILL TIMES IMPROVE, DIRECTION CONFIRMED
sports.body: The fort's emergency drill saw dwarves reach the burrow in record time. Organisers have also confirmed, at last, that the burrow should be above the danger, not below it. The new burrow has a tavern. Attendance is excellent.

sports.head: TRAINING WITH ONE: THE CAPTAIN'S CAMP
sports.body: The militia captain held an open training camp. Nobody came. He sparred with a training dummy, then with a second dummy, then he sparred both dummies against each other and refereed. 'Good session,' he said. 'Solid turnout.'

sports.head: {citizen} WINS THE MUG RACE
sports.body: {citizen} has won the annual mug race, carrying a full mug from the cellar to the far end of the fort without spilling or drinking a drop. Officials are in awe. Historians call it the first time a drink has ever reached a thirsty dwarf.

sports.head: {promoted} THROWS OUT FIRST BALL
sports.body: Newly promoted {promoted} ceremonially opened the season by throwing the first ball, which bounced off three armor stands and into the garbage pit. Nobody went to fetch it. Everyone has learned that lesson.

sports.head: {dogs} DOGS ENTER HUNTING TRIALS
sports.body: All {dogs} of the fort's dogs entered the hunting trials. With meat scarce, they hunted with unusual passion. The trial was won by a dog that caught a rabbit and refused to share. The rabbit has been entered into the record books.

sports.head: {cats} CATS DISRUPT MATCH
sports.body: A match was abandoned after all {cats} cats occupied the pitch and refused to leave. Players tried coaxing, bribing and ignoring them. The cats won on forfeit. The cats are now unbeaten in the league.

sports.head: {stone} SHOT PUT FINAL
sports.body: The {stone} shot put final was hard-fought, with the winner throwing a boulder clean across the dining hall. The Overseer has ordered the boulder smoothed, then engraved, then smoothed again. It will be ready in roughly a year.

sports.head: {drinks}-MUG CHALLENGE POSTPONED
sports.body: The challenge to drink from all {drinks} drinks in the cellars has been postponed, on medical advice, to a later date and to a larger group. The cellars were relieved. The challengers were less so.

sports.head: DRY SEASON SUSPENDS LEAGUE
sports.body: With drink stocks low, league fixtures are off and players have been asked to locate the cellar and stand near it. Several players have taken the opportunity to remember where the well is. Others are simply guarding the brewer.

sports.head: MEAT-SEEKING RACE: NO FINISHERS
sports.body: In a meatless season, runners were sent to find a single piece of meat anywhere in the fort. Nine hours later, the dogs returned with a bone of uncertain origin. The judges declined to award the medal. The dogs ate it.

sports.head: MIGRANTS GIVEN TRYOUTS
sports.body: New arrivals took part in the fort's traditional welcome tryouts: find the tavern, avoid the trees, and learn which burrow not to shelter in. Most passed. One was found asking a liaison for directions and has been placed in remedial orientation.

sports.head: CARAVAN GUARDS CHALLENGE OUR MILITIA
sports.body: The caravan's guards challenged our militia to a friendly bout. The militia, being one captain, agreed to fight them in turn. He fought valiantly, lost seven times and won once against a guard who slipped on the mist ring. 'A win is a win,' he said.

sports.head: SNOW TOURNAMENT: SNOWBALLS, THEN SHOVELS
sports.body: The winter tournament began with a snowball fight and ended when someone realised the depot was buried and the liaison was coming. Players switched to shovels. The liaison arrived anyway and much was shared.

sports.head: SPRING OPEN: TREE LADDER RACE
sports.body: Racers built ladders down from every tree near the gate before any miner could climb one. The winning team finished in an hour. Not a single miner was stranded this spring. The trees are said to be disappointed.

sports.head: SUMMER GAMES: WATER STATIONS EVERY THREE STEPS
sports.body: After historical incidents, the summer games now feature a water station every three steps. Runners must drink at each one. The marathon took four days. Every runner finished. Every runner needed the privy. A sporting triumph.

sports.head: AUTUMN HARVEST RACE COUNTS PLANTS TWICE
sports.body: The harvest race rewards whichever team gathers the most plants. This year both teams counted the same plants. Judges awarded the trophy to the farmers, who had grown them, and who had been ignored by both teams.

sports.head: WINTER INDOOR LEAGUE MOVES TO CISTERN
sports.body: With the surface frozen, the winter league has moved to the edge of the cistern, where players compete in 'ladle accuracy'. The winner drained the most water into the most mugs. Spectators were delighted to be paid in water.

sports.head: THE ARMOR STAND DECATHLON
sports.body: Events: lifting an armor stand, carrying an armor stand, throwing an armor stand, hiding an armor stand from the Overseer, and six more variations. The Overseer won the hiding event by making two hundred more while everyone was distracted.

sports.head: HAMMERER POST REMAINS UNCONTESTED
sports.body: The fort's tryouts for hammerer drew no entrants for the third year. Officials cite 'the job description'. The hammer itself has been entered into the decorative arts competition, where it won a ribbon for being 'unused'.

sports.head: FORGOTTEN BEAST ENTERS STAIR RACE
sports.body: A forgotten beast entered the hundred-level stair race uninvited and set a course record. Dwarven runners abandoned the race and set a new record in a different direction. The beast has been disqualified for not being forgotten.

sports.head: GREAT REWIND RUINS PHOTO FINISH
sports.body: The final of the sprint was decided by a hair when the world blinked and the race restarted. In the replay, a different dwarf won. Both now claim victory. The judges have asked the gods for a clearer ruling.

sports.head: THE OLD FORT DERBY
sports.body: Teams raced the length of the old road to the ruins of {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}. All teams turned back at the gate. 'Ghosts,' said one runner. 'Barrels,' said another. 'Both,' said the third. The trophy stays home.

sports.head: {record_fort} CHALLENGE: CAN YOU BEAT {record}?
sports.body: A charity event invited workshops to beat the infamous {record} of {record_fort}. Nobody tried. Organisers called it 'the most successful event we have ever run'. The money raised was spent on cancelling work orders.

sports.head: CAPTURED {enemy_race} REFEREE LEAVES MATCH
sports.body: A {enemy_race} prisoner, offered freedom if he could referee one match fairly, gave seven red cards in the first minute, all to dwarves. He has been returned to his cell, where he is said to be 'happier'. {enemy} declined to comment.

sports.head: {civ} GAMES: OUR FORT FINISHES SECOND-LAST
sports.body: At the games of {civ}, our athletes placed second-last overall, ahead only of a fort that sent a single militia captain. Officials have pointed out that we, too, sent a single militia captain. He was very tired.

sports.head: {monarch} SENDS TROPHY; IT IS A THRONE
sports.body: {monarch} has sent the fort a trophy for 'endurance'. It is a throne. The fort already has several. It has been placed at the end of the row. Nobody can now tell which throne is the trophy, including the monarch's envoy.

sports.head: {liaison} REFEREES, SHARES MUCH
sports.body: {liaison} agreed to referee the cup final and stopped play every five minutes to tell both teams there was much to share. The match lasted nine hours. By the end, both teams had signed import agreements. Nobody scored.

sports.head: BARREL-ROLLING: STILL BESIDE THE BEDS
sports.body: Competitors rolled barrels from the cellar toward the bedrooms, in support of the 'still beside the beds' campaign. Twelve barrels arrived. Eleven dwarves drank them on arrival. The campaign calls this 'a strong proof of concept'.

sports.head: LEVER RELAY FLOODS THE MIST RING
sports.body: In the lever relay, one runner pulled every lever in the fort, flooding the mist ring, raising a bridge and opening the cistern gates. Nobody won. Everyone had a lovely day. The engineers have taken the levers away.

sports.head: DOG POLO SUSPENDED AFTER ONE CHUKKA
sports.body: Dogs were ridden by dwarves in the first match of dog polo. The dogs had other ideas, most of which involved the kitchen. The match ended in the larder with no goals and one very happy dog.

sports.head: THE QUIET-WALK PAST THE LIAISON
sports.body: Contestants tried to walk past the visiting liaison's office without being invited in to discuss imports. The record is two steps. The winner wore a disguise and carried a cat. He was still asked about rings.

sports.head: FISHING CONTEST: CARP 3, DWARVES 0
sports.body: The fishing contest ended with three dwarves pulled into the river and no fish caught. The carp were awarded the match on goal difference. A rematch has been proposed by the carp, via splashing.

sports.head: THE PUMP PULL: A TEST OF STAMINA
sports.body: Pump operators competed to work the mist pumps longest without stopping. The winner pumped for sixteen hours. Spectators in the spray were the happiest in the fort's history. The winner has not yet regained feeling in his arms.

sports.head: BED-RACE THROUGH THE HOSPITAL
sports.body: Patients raced their beds through the hospital corridors in a charity event. The hospital has no doctor this week, so nobody objected. The winner reached the far end and immediately needed treatment, which was not available.

sports.head: THRONE-CARRY: THE STRONGEST DWARF CONTEST
sports.body: Strongdwarves carried surplus thrones from storage to the dining hall. The winner carried six. The losers carried one each. The dining hall now has too many thrones. The Overseer has ordered more tables, very many.

sports.head: GOBLIN-SPOTTING TOURNAMENT A SUCCESS
sports.body: Lookouts competed to spot the first goblin on the horizon. The winner spotted forty, approaching. The tournament was promptly converted into a defence drill. The militia was informed. The militia was off duty.

sports.head: GEM COUNT SPEED TRIAL
sports.body: Clerks raced to count the fort's gems. One finished in an hour, one in two, and the third was interrupted by a jeweler cutting them faster than he could count. The judges have accepted 'a lot' as an official number.

sports.head: MOOD WATCH: BETTING ON THE NEXT FEY
sports.body: Bookmakers are offering odds on which dwarf will next be taken by a strange mood and what they will demand. Rough gems are the favourite. Plant cloth is a strong second. 'Whatever we just ran out of' is listed as a sure thing.

sports.head: {citizen} TAKES SILVER IN LIFTING
sports.body: {citizen} took silver in the lifting event, raising a full barrel over their head and then, unexpectedly, drinking from it mid-lift. Judges deducted points for style but applauded the hydration. A sensible athlete.

sports.head: SEARABBEYS MEMORIAL MUG RACE
sports.body: Held in memory of Bomrek Enshalcatten, who died of thirst at Searabbeys beside 1,994 drinks, the race asks runners to carry one mug to one dwarf. This year, for the first time, the mug arrived full. Spectators wept into their own mugs.

sports.head: QUAKEFOCUS CUP: 1,981 ARMOR STANDS SLALOM
sports.body: The traditional Quakefocus Cup returned with its famous course through all 1,981 armor stands. The record holder took a wrong turn at stand 600 and emerged at the throne room, where he was crowned 148 times.

sports.head: GOBLINS OF SEARABBEYS CHALLENGE US
sports.body: The Torments of Hating, who occupy Searabbeys, have challenged us to a match on their home ground. We have declined. They have offered to bring The Nuanced Hamlet as a trophy. We are reconsidering.

sports.head: CHASTE CUDGEL WINS CUDGEL TOURNAMENT
sports.body: To nobody's surprise, The Chaste Cudgel won the regional cudgel tournament. Bomrek Thimshursåkzul accepted the trophy and immediately used it to dust Tametomb. The Oily Boots came last after slipping in the opening round.

sports.head: AMUSING DUTIES TOURNAMENT ATTRACTS 48 CLAIMANTS
sports.body: A tournament to settle the ownership of The Amusing Duties drew all forty-eight living claimants. Nobody brought the greaves, which are at Fieryaged. The tournament ended in a draw and forty-eight sulks.

sports.head: CELLAR ORIENTEERING: FIND THE BARREL
sports.body: Competitors were blindfolded, spun around and asked to find the nearest barrel. The winner found one in under a minute, by smell. The slowest walked past four barrels and was found at the top of a tree. The league has added ropes.

sports.head: NINE-PIN BOWLING WITH EMPTY PLACES
sports.body: The militia captain has invented a new sport: he bowls at nine pins, one for each empty place in his squad. He knocks down all nine every time. 'It's therapeutic,' he says. Applications to join the squad remain at zero.

sports.head: CARAVAN-UNLOADING SPEED RECORD
sports.body: Haulers set a new record unloading a caravan, finishing before the liaison could finish saying there was much to share. Merchants were stunned. The liaison finished his sentence anyway, in an empty depot, to a confused yak.

sports.head: GHOST WRESTLING CANCELLED, GHOST UPSET
sports.body: The catacomb ghost had signed up for the wrestling open but was ruled ineligible on the grounds of being incorporeal. It has haunted the referee every night since. The referee has asked to be ruled ineligible too.

sports.head: THE ENGRAVING SPRINT
sports.body: Engravers raced to decorate a single smoothed wall. The winner carved a dwarf being struck by a carp in nine minutes. The runner-up carved an armor stand, then another, then was gently stopped by friends before it became a work order.

sports.head: BEST-KEPT BURROW AWARD GOES TO TAVERN
sports.body: The judges toured every burrow in the fort for the Best-Kept Burrow award and gave it to the tavern, which is not a burrow but was where the judges ended up. No burrow called 'Safety' was considered, at the judges' request.

weather_jokes.text: Rain on the surface. The Overseer has dispatched plant gatherers to every corner of the map, because nothing says harvest like wet strawberries.
Rain again. Somewhere up there a miner is sitting in a tree, getting rained on, and still not drinking it.
It is raining, which means the elves are grateful, the haulers are damp and the depot cloth is ruined. Business as usual.
Rain forecast all week. Dwarves are reminded that rain is free water, and that standing in it with your mouth open is undignified but legal.
Wet weather above. Below, the mist ring keeps everyone just as damp, but happier about it.
Rain. The refuse pile on the surface has never smelled more like itself.
Snow on the surface. The trees are frozen and, for once, nobody is up them.
Snow, and lots of it. The depot is buried, the caravan is late and the liaison is somehow still on time.
A blizzard above. Brave plant gatherers are still out, by order. Their bravery is being measured in toes.
Snowfall heavy. Dwarves are reminded that snow is technically water, and that eating it is still better than dying of thirst.
Snow. The garbage pit is blanketed white, and for one beautiful morning it looks like a field of flour.
Snowed in. The tavern is full, the barrels are near and, for the first time in history, nobody is thirsty.
Clear skies. Perfect weather for a miner to wander outside, look at a tree, and think, dangerously, 'I could get up there.'
Not a cloud above. The windmills are still. Nobody is sure if this matters. Nobody ever is.
Clear and bright. Goblin scouts can see a very long way today. So can we, which makes it a fair day for once.
Sunny on the surface. The Overseer is said to have ordered the sky smoothed.
Clear weather, dry air. The almanac recommends knowing where the nearest barrel is at all times, just in case.
Lovely clear day. The elf caravan is taking the scenic route, which is all of it.
Spring: the thaw sets the rivers running, the carp grumbling and the miners eyeing fresh green branches.
Spring blooms on the surface. The Overseer has queued gathering jobs for every single flower.
Summer heat on the surface. Please drink something. Anything. Please. History is watching.
Summer sun. The mist ring has never been more popular, or more crowded, or more damp.
Autumn leaves falling, and the trees look lighter. A miner has taken this as an invitation. Somebody stop him.
Autumn wind rattles the windmills. They turn faster. Still nobody knows what for.
Winter: the cistern is the warmest place in the fort to stand and the coldest place to fall in.
Winter settles in. The militia captain has declared the weather 'too cold for duty'. Also too warm. Also just right.
{weather} on the surface, {season} in the hearts of the miners, and the barrels as full and far away as ever.
{weather} above. Below: the usual. Rock, ale, an Overseer with a plan.
Today's weather: {weather}. Today's forecast for the Safety burrow: do not go down there.
{weather} in {fort} today. The plant gatherers have been sent out regardless. They always are.
Weather in year {year}: mostly sky, some rain, and one miner in a tree who refuses to discuss either.
{season} forecast: overcast with a chance of work orders. Heavy armor stands possible by evening.
Forecast: drizzle near the pumps, otherwise dry. Dwarves are reminded that dry is how this always begins.
Weather report: unknown. Our forecaster went up to check, climbed a tree to see better, and has not come down.
Thunder overhead. The dwarves cannot hear it. The cats can. The cats have filed a complaint with the mayor.
The forecast calls for goblins, heavy in places, clearing by spring if the walls hold.
High pressure over the surface. Low pressure in the smoothing department, where three dwarves face sixteen thousand walls.
Fog over the depot. The liaison has emerged from it, saying there is much to share. The fog was better.
Wind from the east, smelling of the refuse pile. Wind from the west, smelling of elves. We prefer the east.
Mild weather. A good day for anything except climbing, hauling out of pits or sheltering thirty levels down.
Today: a chance of strange moods, increasing toward evening. Hide one rough gem, just in case.
The world blinked overnight. If the weather seems familiar, it is because you have already had it.
Rain over the cellars? No. The cellars are underground. That is the point of cellars. And yet, somehow, the miner is still thirsty.
Drinks are plentiful at {drinks}, so the weather can do as it likes. Nobody in this fort will die of thirst today. Probably.
Low drink stocks and a dry wind. Brewers are on double shifts and the well has been given a guard.
{weather} over the ruins of {past_fort}. They lasted {past_fort_years}. The weather there has lasted longer.
{weather} over {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}. The ghosts are said to like this kind of weather.
Weather forecast for {record_fort}: cloudy, with a high chance of {record}. Still.
{weather} over the camps of {enemy}. We hope it is very wet over there. We hope it is wetter.
Storm warning: {enemy_race} raiders, gusting to forty, moving in from the dark fortress.
{weather} in the capital of {civ}, where {monarch} is said to be indoors, on the one throne.
{liaison} reports the roads are dry. He has much more to share about the roads. Please do not ask.
Rain over Searabbeys. The Torments of Hating are using the 1,994 drinks as roof weights.
Snow over Quakefocus, gently settling on 1,981 armor stands and 148 thrones, like dust that cares.
Clear skies over Fieryaged, where The Amusing Duties lie unworn. Ideal weather for claimant number forty-nine.
Fog over Shadyghosts. Omo Fewethauyira cannot be seen. That is the bad news.
Dark at The Sable Nights, as always. Thone Nìnoana reports the weather is lovely.
Wind over Padtufted, Pulledrained and Ironcrowds, carrying the sound of The Crazed Hex, crazed.
